tickets.text:
Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync

During the overnight CustomerSync batch window (scheduled 01:00–04:00 PST), the Integration Gateway in us-west-2 began returning repeated 504 Gateway Timeout errors and API call durations exceeding 30 seconds when calling the downstream CRM API endpoint at api.customersync.corplabs.com. This was first reported by Priya Nair (Application Support lead, Portland office) after the Reporting Dashboard failed to refresh overnight customer records. Gateway logs on host INTGW-WEST-01.corplabs.internal showed a token refresh job failure (job ID: tknrot-20251201-0130) in the same time window, indicating the sync process was blocked by downstream authentication issues rather than a general platform outage. Approximately 14,200 customer records were delayed, impacting dependent reporting and sync workflows used by the finance reconciliation team.

API integration timeouts causing delayed data sync

Overnight scheduled data synchronization jobs between the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east.corplabs.internal) and the downstream Inventory API service intermittently failed from approximately 02:00 to 03:30 UTC on 2025-12-02 in us-east-1. The gateway received repeated 504 Gateway Timeout and ETIMEDOUT responses on the /api/v2/inventory/sync endpoint, which delayed application data updates and increased integration job failures. Reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Chicago operations center — internal operations needed the scheduled sync process to complete normally so downstream application records would be current by the start of business.

Integration Gateway - scheduled job timeouts

Overnight scheduled data sync jobs through the Integration Gateway in Kubernetes (namespace: intg-gateway-prod) began failing against the upstream partner API (partner: Meridian Data Services) in us-east-1. The issue was first flagged by the Monitoring System at 2025-12-02T03:14Z when engineer Priya Narayanan received PagerDuty alerts on repeated HTTP 401 Unauthorized responses with token expiration indicators from the gateway pod intg-gw-pod-7b4c running on host WORKSTATION-INTGW-PN. These were followed by HTTP 504 timeouts as the gateway retried until backoff limits were reached. The failures delayed expected partner data synchronization for internal API clients (service account: svc-datasync-east) during the 02:00–05:00 UTC scheduled job window. Reported by Marcus Ellison (emp ID: EMP-90274) from the Denver integration operations team.

Integration Gateway timeouts causing delayed data sync to downstream service

Nightly batch data synchronization from DataSyncApp (service account svc-datasync) through the Integration Gateway to the downstream InventoryAPI service began failing between 03:20 and 03:50 UTC on 2025-12-03. The API Service running on pod datasyncapp-worker-7b in namespace appsync-prod (us-east-1) received repeated HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout responses, and at least one scheduled sync job (sync-20251203-batch4) failed, delaying data availability for downstream consumers in the Chicago fulfillment group. Investigation by Marcus Ellison showed the gateway was still referencing a deprecated retry/backoff policy (v1.2) while downstream latency was elevated, causing retries to amplify timeout behavior rather than allowing the batch to complete. Reported initially by Priya Nagarajan via the Application Support on-call channel.
tickets.cause: Deprecated retry/backoff policy causing amplified timeouts

tickets.text:
Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync

Customer-facing integration jobs between the Application and the downstream partner API (PartnerSync endpoint at partner-api.extdata.io) intermittently failed over the last 90 minutes during peak traffic. The Integration Gateway node igw-prod-07 in us-east-1 returned repeated HTTP 504 timeout responses on outbound partner API calls originating from service account svc-integrations, which caused inbound API Service requests to queue on the api-ingest-pool cluster, retries to accumulate, and data synchronization for the nightly billing feed to be delayed rather than completed in the expected 06:00–07:30 UTC window. Reported by Marcus Ellison (emp ID EMP-40821) from the Denver office.

Integration Gateway API calls timing out causing integration job failures

Integration jobs for the reporting application (managed by the Data Integration team under Marcus Delgado) began failing around 09:12 UTC on 2025-12-04 when API calls routed through the Integration Gateway on host INTGW-AKS-PROD-01 started timing out. The issue was first reported by analyst Priya Nair (emp ID DI-40287) who observed delayed real-time data syncs and failed nightly ingestion runs from her workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN (IP 10.42.18.93). Application and gateway logs showed repeated 504 Gateway Timeout errors, and the Monitoring System dashboard indicated rising downstream latency and elevated error responses from the external analytics API endpoint. The outage affected the API integration path used by the reporting application and blocked normal data synchronization for the Austin office until the downstream rate-limit condition was mitigated.

Intermittent API timeouts from Integration Gateway with conflicting token/latency evidence

Scheduled internal batch jobs using the Integration Gateway (gateway cluster igw-prod-east-01) began failing intermittently after a recent deploy (build 4.7.2-rc3, deployed 2025-12-04T03:45Z), causing delayed data synchronization and missed downstream deliveries over an approximately 3-hour window starting around 04:00 UTC. The issue was reported by Marcus Ellison (mellison@corplabs.com) from the Atlanta data operations team, who noticed that several overnight ETL batches tied to service account svc-batch-integ failed to complete. Gateway monitoring showed repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses aligned with elevated downstream service latency on the Order Fulfillment API endpoint (/api/v2/orders/sync). Some client traces from host WORKSTATION-BATCH-ME also showed 401 Unauthorized responses, indicating a secondary token validity issue that complicated diagnosis.

Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync

Nightly integration jobs from the Integration Gateway (pod ig-prod-worker-07 on cluster k8s-east-prod) to the downstream API Service were delayed between 23:50–00:15 UTC on 2025-12-04 in us-east-1. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Dallas application support team after the overnight data synchronization workflow failed to complete on schedule. Monitoring System dashboards showed repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses and 401 token_expired errors originating from service account svc-ig-sync, causing queued sync jobs to fail and data ingestion to lag by over 25 minutes. The blocked task was the overnight data synchronization workflow feeding the Ingestion Worker pipeline, with impact to downstream application data freshness for the finance and analytics consumers until authentication and retry behavior were corrected.

Nightly integration timeouts via Integration Gateway (03:00 UTC)

Nightly batch data sync jobs sent through the Integration Gateway to the downstream partner (Acme Data Services) are failing around 03:00 UTC in us-east-1. The gateway returns 504 Gateway Timeout for POST /sync during the scheduled run window, and monitoring shows a matching latency spike at the same time. This is delaying the partner data synchronization workflow for batch-sync-users. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Dallas integration operations team. Current telemetry is incomplete because request correlation IDs and token rotation history were not available in the original evidence. The affected API client ID is intg-client-batch-7741, and the integration service account username is svc_batchsync. Requests originate from host WORKSTATION-INTGOPS-MD (10.42.18.97).

Intermittent API timeouts from Integration Gateway causing delayed data sync

Application support engineer Priya Nair (emp ID: E-40291) reported delayed synchronization between the CRM Application and the third-party Salesforce Data API beginning around 2025-12-05 09:00 UTC. Intermittent 504 Gateway Timeout responses were returned by the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east.corplabs.internal), causing some scheduled API integration jobs to fail or complete late. Monitoring System dashboards showed correlated spikes in outbound latency from the gateway to the downstream API endpoint https://api.partnersync.io/v2/data. A gateway pod restart on node igw-worker-04 and temporary timeout increase from 30s to 90s did not remove the issue, and available logs on the gateway did not show clear token expiry errors or enough detail to distinguish between rate limiting and downstream latency. Ticket raised from the Arlington office.

Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync

Nightly DataSync integration jobs submitted by the application_support team (contact: r.martinez@corplabs.com) were attempting to send customer records through the Integration Gateway (gateway node igw-prod-east-07) to the downstream API service, but starting around 02:10 UTC on 2025-12-05 the gateway began receiving repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses from the API endpoint and requests exceeded the configured 30 second client timeout. This caused job failures across the DataSync worker pool running on host WORKSTATION-DSYNC-RM, queue growth in the integration worker (queue depth exceeded 4,200 pending messages), and delayed customer data synchronization for the Chicago processing region until retries or manual recovery actions completed. Incident was initially reported by Rafael Martinez (EMP-80241) via the on-call pager.

Integration Gateway timeouts during data sync — expired API token

Scheduled data sync jobs from the application to the downstream API began failing in Kubernetes in us-east-1, triggering monitoring alerts at 2025-12-06 02:14 UTC. The Integration Gateway (host: INTGW-NODE-04) showed repeated request timeouts and 504 Gateway Timeout responses, with accompanying 401 Unauthorized errors. This blocked normal DataSync Service processing for the Chicago data center and caused delayed data synchronization for affected users and dependent systems. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Jennings (emp ID: EMP-40821) via email at mjennings@corplabs.com.

API calls to third-party timing out via Integration Gateway

Internal integration users on the data-ops team (reported by Marcus Delgado, emp ID EMP-40291) were trying to run overnight data syncs through the Integration Gateway (gateway node igw-prod-east-07) to a third-party vendor API (vendor: Nextera Data Services) in Kubernetes us-east-1, but requests intermittently stalled for 30-60 seconds and returned 504 Gateway Timeout responses. Multiple integration jobs failed — specifically jobs SYNC-4401, SYNC-4402, and SYNC-4405 — and data synchronization to the downstream CRM pipeline was delayed. The issue was observed starting around 09:30 UTC from workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MDELGADO (IP 10.42.17.88), with no confirmed recent application deployment, and token rotation history for service account svc-integ-nextera was initially unclear.

Integration Gateway API timeouts impacting data sync

Users reported failed scheduled integration jobs and delayed data synchronization for the API Integration used by the Order Processing App. During the past hour, the Integration Gateway in Kubernetes (us-east-1) showed a spike in HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout responses along with intermittent 401 Unauthorized errors, preventing normal authenticated API calls and delaying downstream data updates. The issue was initially flagged by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Austin office, who noticed that order sync jobs for client account OP-4417 were stalling. Additional reports came in from Priya Nair (emp ID: E-20587) confirming the same behavior from the Portland office.

Integration Gateway API calls timing out and returning authorization errors

During the nightly synchronization window starting at 02:00 UTC on 2025-12-07, internal applications routed through the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east.corpsync.internal) were unable to complete downstream API data sync jobs. The issue was first flagged by Rajesh Menon from the platform engineering team after the HR data pipeline and finance reconciliation feeds both failed. Monitoring dashboards on the Monitoring System and gateway access logs showed repeated HTTP 401 Unauthorized responses from the downstream API endpoint (api.dataservices.corpsync.internal/v2/sync), followed by cascading API call timeouts at the 30-second threshold. This increased job failure rates across 14 scheduled integration tasks and delayed data synchronization for multiple internal consumers including payroll and inventory services. Investigation by the application team focused on authentication token health and downstream API availability, ultimately determining that the gateway service account token (svc-igw-sync) had exceeded its 30-day rotation window by 15 days.

Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data syncs

Scheduled data sync jobs through the Integration Gateway (namespace: intg-gateway-prod, cluster: k8s-east-prod-04) began failing or queuing at approximately 09:12 UTC on 2025-12-08 because POST requests to the downstream API Service endpoint https://api-svc.corplabs.internal/v2/sync were returning repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Application Support team in the Charlotte office, noting that data lag for the integration workflow in the Kubernetes environment in us-east-1 had exceeded 45 minutes and was blocking timely completion of routine sync processing for the customer-data pipeline. Investigation focused on whether the failures were caused by expired authentication tokens, API rate limiting, or elevated downstream response latency. Ticket was assigned to senior integration engineer Priya Nair (emp ID: EMP-40821) for triage.

Integration Gateway API timeouts causing PaymentSync failures

PaymentSync backfill and scheduled synchronization jobs intermittently failed between 02:10 and 02:40 UTC on 2025-12-08 when the Integration Gateway (gateway-prod-east-07.payments.internal) timed out while calling the downstream payment API endpoint at https://api.payments.internal/v2/sync. This caused queued sync work on the paymentsync-worker pods in the us-east-1 Kubernetes cluster, delayed payment data updates for Finance Users, and repeated 504 timeout responses logged by the gateway. The issue was initially reported by Rajesh Menon (rmenon@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office after the PaymentSyncApp dashboard showed stalled jobs. Immediate recovery was observed after token rotation by ops engineer Lisa Cheng, but available validation evidence did not show token expiry, so the incident is best explained as downstream latency with token rotation treated as a coincidental or non-causal mitigation.

Integration Gateway API requests timing out

During the nightly customer sync window starting 2025-12-10 03:00 UTC, clients calling the Integration Gateway (gw-prod-east.corpsync.internal) experienced intermittent 504 Gateway Timeout errors and failed integration jobs. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office, noting that the Customer Sync Service and Billing App feeds were stalling. The issue affected customer data synchronization for dependent applications, with the Monitoring System dashboard showing elevated gateway response times (p95 > 4.2s) and downstream API latency on the Order Fulfillment API. Authentication failures (ERR_AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID) were also observed early in the event around 03:12 UTC, but token rotation on service account svc-custsync only reduced those errors temporarily and did not eliminate the timeout pattern. Downstream host api-orders.corpsync.internal was identified as the slow responder.

Intermittent API timeouts from Integration Gateway to downstream API

Scheduled integration jobs and live API calls from Integration Gateway v3.2 in us-east-1 began failing after about 03:10 UTC on 2025-12-11 with 504 Gateway Timeout responses and elevated downstream latency. The issue was first reported by integration admin rchandra (Rajesh Chandra, emp ID EMP-40821) from the Arlington office, who noticed that the nightly order-sync job and real-time inventory push to the downstream Fulfillment API were returning ERR_API_TIMEOUT. Retries were exhausted after the default 3-attempt cycle, delaying data synchronization across dependent systems and preventing normal API integration processing until the downstream performance issue was corrected. Alerts were firing on the Monitoring System dashboard for gateway node igw-east-node04 (10.42.18.77) and the issue was visible from the submitter's workstation WORKSTATION-RCHANDRA at 10.200.5.34.
tickets.cause: Intermittent API timeouts due to downstream latency

tickets.text:
Orders sync failing

Scheduled order-sync processing (job: order-sync-prod-batch-7a) to the external API through the Integration Gateway began failing around 2025-12-12 03:40 UTC with repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (order-processing team lead) after downstream order data failed to appear in the external fulfillment system. Retries are not draining the backlog — queue depth reached ~4,200 pending records on pod order-sync-worker-6d8f4 in us-east-1. Impact is limited by manual retry handling initiated by mdelgado from workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD (10.42.18.93), but the sync workflow remains blocked until gateway timeout behavior, token validity, and possible downstream latency or rate limiting are verified. Contact: mdelgado@corplabs.com / ext 4-7831.

Integration Gateway API timeouts to Billing API causing delayed data sync

Automated monitoring detected that Integration Gateway requests to the Billing API in us-east-1 began timing out around 2025-12-12T09:40:00Z. Outbound calls from integration node INTGW-PROD-04 (10.22.18.97) returned repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses and some requests exceeded the 30 second timeout window, causing integration jobs to fail and delaying customer billing data synchronization. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the AppIntegrationTeam in Charlotte. The issue affected API-based sync processing on Kubernetes (EKS) and created downstream data freshness impact until Billing API latency was reduced. Ticket opened on behalf of the integration operations group by agent Priya Nair (EMP-40821).

Expired TLS certificate on Internal Web Service behind Load Balancer

Internal users and dependent services were trying to reach the svc-internal endpoint (svc-internal.corplabs.internal) over TLS through the load balancer LB-EAST-02, but clients began showing certificate warnings and rejecting the connection. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office, who noticed that requests from her workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MC were returning NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID errors. The load balancer presented an expired certificate (CN=svc-internal.corplabs.internal, expired 2025-12-10T00:00:00Z) and an incomplete chain after the renewal window was missed, which blocked normal access to the internal web service and caused TLS handshake failures for internal integrations in us-east-1. Multiple teams including the payroll integration service (contact: David Ortiz, emp ID E-40291) confirmed downstream failures.

Expired TLS certificate caused internal service TLS outage

Users and internal integrations were trying to access the Internal Web Service at internal-web.svc.cluster.local, but browsers showed certificate warnings and dependent API calls began failing TLS validation. The issue was first reported by platform engineer Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the Austin office at approximately 05:15 UTC. Monitoring detected TLS handshake failures from multiple client IPs including 10.42.17.88, and load balancer logs on LB-EAST-01 showed an expired certificate was being presented, causing an internal service outage until the certificate chain on the load balancer was corrected.

Internal Web Service TLS outage

Internal staff in the Arlington data center were trying to access the Internal Web Service over HTTPS for the internal-service-api and internal-dashboard endpoints (internal-service.company.local), but browsers showed certificate warnings and requests through the F5 load balancer (lb-prod-east-01.company.local) failed TLS negotiation. Users could not reach the service securely, and monitoring reported TLS handshake failures and 502 responses in us-east-1-dc1 after the service certificate passed its expiration on 2025-12-13 without the renewed chain being deployed. Initially reported by Maria Castillo (mcastillo@company.local) from the Finance team, who was unable to load the internal dashboard from her workstation WORKSTATION-MC-FIN.

Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage

Users were trying to access the Internal Web Service (https://appportal.corplabs.internal) through the internal nginx load balancer at lb-web-east.corplabs.internal, but browsers showed expired-certificate warnings (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) and dependent clients failed TLS handshakes. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen from the Austin office at approximately 04:20 UTC on 2025-12-14. The service became unavailable over TLS because the presented certificate (CN=appportal.corplabs.internal, issued by CorpLabs Internal CA) had passed its expiration date of 2025-12-13 and the updated certificate chain had not been deployed on the load balancer, blocking normal internal application access for the internal_users group.

Expired TLS certificate causing Internal Web Service TLS outage

Users and internal systems were trying to reach internal.example.com over TLS, but the load balancer lb-int-01 presented an expired certificate and browsers showed certificate date warnings. Multiple teams reported the issue starting around 21:45 UTC, including the DevOps integration pipeline managed by rchen and the monitoring dashboard used by the Portland operations team. Dependent integrations (including the inventory sync service running on WORKSTATION-DEVOPS-RC) also began failing TLS handshakes with NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID, making the internal web service unavailable over HTTPS. The outage aligns with the certificate expiration date of 2025-12-14 after the automated renewal job (cert-renewal-scheduler, last configured by mwatkins) did not run and no renewal alert was raised. Ticket submitted by Danielle Ortiz (dortiz@corplabs.com, EMP-40821) on behalf of the internal_services user group.

Expired TLS certificate on Internal Web Service caused TLS outages behind load

Internal users and dependent services were trying to access internal.example.corp, but the endpoint began presenting an expired TLS certificate and browser certificate warnings (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) while integrations failed TLS handshakes. The outage was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office, noting that the Internal Web Service behind load balancer LB-EAST-02 was unreachable over HTTPS. The certificate expiration window had passed as of 2025-12-15 03:14 UTC, blocking normal internal application access for all users in the us-east-1 region until the deployed certificate chain on the load balancer was corrected.

Expired TLS certificate on Internal Web Service causing TLS outages

Users in the Charlotte office were trying to access the Internal Web Service at https://internalapp.corplabs.com over HTTPS, but browsers displayed certificate warnings (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) and dependent clients failed TLS negotiation. The outage was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) early this morning around 02:45 UTC after the service certificate expired on 2025-12-16T00:00:00Z. The load balancer (LB-EAST-CLUSTER-01) continued presenting the old expired certificate chain, preventing normal access to the internal application for all internal_users in the us-east-1-dc1 region.

Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage

Internal users and automated health checks were unable to reach the internal dashboard at https://internal.example.com starting around 02:00 UTC on 2025-12-16. Browsers displayed an expired certificate warning (ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) and dependent API clients from the DevOps team failed TLS handshakes. The issue was initially reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office, who noticed the dashboard was inaccessible over HTTPS. Automated Nagios checks from host MONITOR-EAST-01 also flagged the endpoint. The service was completely unavailable over TLS for internal teams, blocking normal dashboard access, CI/CD pipeline status views, and deployment tracking until the expired service certificate and load balancer certificate chain were corrected.

Expired TLS certificate resurfaced on internal web service

Users were trying to reach the internal HTTPS service at https://internal-api.corp and related internal applications, but browsers displayed certificate warnings and TLS connections failed starting this morning. The issue was first reported by Marcus Chen from the Portland office, who noticed that the internal-admin-portal was unreachable over TLS. The service renewal had previously been performed, but access was blocked because the load balancer was still presenting an expired certificate chain even though the backend had a newer certificate. Additional reports came in from developers including Priya Nair and Tom Galloway, confirming the same behavior across multiple workstations.
tickets.cause: Expired TLS certificate on load balancer

tickets.text:
Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage

Users and internal integrations were trying to access the Internal Web Service at https://portal.internal.corplabs.com through the load balancer (LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal), but browsers displayed NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID warnings and dependent API calls from services owned by the Platform Engineering team failed TLS negotiation. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40291) from the Denver office at approximately 02:05 UTC on 2025-12-17. The service became unavailable over TLS after the presented certificate (CN=portal.internal.corplabs.com, issued by CorpLabs Internal CA) passed its validity window on 2025-12-16T23:59:59Z, and the load balancer continued serving an outdated certificate chain containing an expired intermediate, blocking normal internal application access for all users in the us-east-1 environment.

Expired TLS certificate caused Internal Web Service TLS outages

Internal users and monitoring systems were trying to reach the Internal Web Service at https://appportal.corp.internal over HTTPS, but beginning around 2025-12-17 08:12 UTC the service presented certificate warnings and failed TLS handshakes. The issue was first reported by Danielle Ortega (dortega@corp.internal) from the Austin office, who received NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID errors in her browser. The load balancer LB-CENTRAL-01.corp.internal continued serving an expired certificate and outdated chain after renewal was missed, blocking normal access to the internal application and causing service unavailability over TLS for approximately 150 internal users.

Internal Web Service TLS certificate expired, causing TLS warnings and service unavailability

Users were trying to access the internal web service at internal.websvc.corp starting around 2025-12-18 08:12 UTC, but browsers displayed NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID warnings and TLS connections failed. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40291) from the Chicago office, who noticed the certificate warning while accessing the HR onboarding portal served behind internal.websvc.corp. Internal health checks running from health-checker on the Kubernetes cluster in us-east-1 also began returning 502 errors on TLS backend probes, preventing normal access to the service from inside the network. The load balancer (lb-prod-east-01.infra.corp) was still presenting a stale certificate bundle with an incomplete chain, which compounded the issue until both the certificate and chain were corrected.

Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage

Internal users and automated health checks were trying to reach the service-catalog endpoint (https://service-catalog.corplabs.internal) over HTTPS, but beginning around 2025-12-18T08:12Z the service presented an expired certificate and browser trust warnings. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40291) from the Arlington office, who noticed the certificate warning while accessing the catalog from her workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MC. Clients saw TLS validation failures, including browser certificate warnings and failed handshake checks from multiple internal IPs including 10.22.4.87, which blocked normal access to the internal web service until the certificate and chain were corrected on the load balancer and service endpoint.

Expired TLS certificate on Internal Web Service causing TLS failures (Load Balancer

Users were trying to access the internal web service (internal-web.corplabs.internal) over HTTPS, but browsers displayed certificate warnings and dependent clients failed TLS validation. The internal-web-service became unavailable over TLS in the Richmond data center after the service certificate expired on 2025-12-17, and the Load Balancer (LB-EAST-02.corplabs.internal) was serving an incomplete chain. This was first reported by Marcus Delgado (emp ID E-40821) via the IT portal. The issue blocked normal internal service access for the internal-services user group until the certificate and chain were corrected.

Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage

Internal users and monitoring were trying to reach svc-internal-web through the ALB (alb-prod-east-01.corplabs.internal), but starting around 08:15 UTC on 2025-12-19 the service began failing TLS handshakes and showing certificate warnings. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office, who noticed NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID errors in Chrome when accessing https://svc-internal-web.corplabs.internal. Dependent internal clients including the internal-admin-portal could not establish secure connections, causing the internal web service to be unavailable over TLS in us-east-1. Additional reports came in from employees in the Raleigh office confirming the same behavior.

Expired TLS certificate on Internal Web Service causing HTTPS outage

Internal users in the Denver office were trying to access the internal web service at https://internal.service.local, but browsers displayed certificate expiration warnings and automated health checks began failing TLS handshakes. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID EMP-40821) via the IT portal. The service was effectively unavailable over HTTPS after the certificate passed its renewal window on 2025-12-18, blocking normal internal application access for approximately 150 users in the internal-users group until the certificate and presented chain were corrected on the load balancer (lb-prod-central-01.infra.local).

Expired TLS certificate on Load Balancer causing internal web service TLS failures

Users were trying to access the internal web service at https://internal.corplabs.com, but browsers displayed certificate warnings (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) and internal API clients failed TLS handshakes. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (EMP-40291) from the Portland office at approximately 17:45 UTC on 2025-12-19. The service was effectively unavailable over HTTPS because the TLS certificate presented by the F5 Big-IP load balancer lb-prod-01.corplabs.internal in us-east-1 had expired at 2025-12-19T04:00Z, impacting all internal services relying on that endpoint until the certificate and full chain were replaced.

Expired TLS certificate on load balancer causing internal service TLS failures

Users and internal clients were trying to access the internal-api service through the corporate load balancer (haproxy-lb-01.corp.local), but browsers displayed certificate expiration warnings and dependent integrations failed TLS handshakes. The outage was first reported by Marcus Jennings (emp ID E-40821) from the Portland office at approximately 05:30 UTC. The certificate presented for internal-api.corp.local had expired and the load balancer continued serving the old CA-signed chain, blocking normal access to the internal web service for the internal-devs user group.
tickets.cause: Expired TLS certificate on load balancer

tickets.text:
Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage

Internal developers on the Platform Engineering team were trying to access the internal API at https://internal.example.corp/v2/services over HTTPS, but browsers began showing certificate warnings and automated clients (including CI/CD pipelines running on WORKSTATION-BUILD-MK) started failing TLS handshakes at approximately 07:15 UTC on 2025-12-20. The affected endpoint was internal.example.corp behind load balancer LB-EAST-02.infra.example.corp, which made the internal web service unreachable over TLS and blocked normal API calls for the entire Arlington development group. Monitoring did not alert before the outage — the certificate-management-service renewal job configured by r.navarro had not fired its 30-day pre-expiry notification. Renewal response was delayed until developer Priya Chandrasekaran (emp ID EMP-40821) reported the issue and the expired certificate being served by the load balancer was confirmed by the infrastructure team.

Expired TLS certificate caused Internal Web Service TLS outage — certificate renewed

Internal users and dependent integrations across the Portland datacenter were trying to reach the Internal Web Service at https://appportal.corp.internal, but the endpoint began failing TLS validation after the service certificate expired on 2025-12-20. Browsers showed certificate warnings and clients reported ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID, TLS handshake failures, and some 502 responses over TLS. The issue was initially reported by Maria Chen (emp ID EMP-40291) from the internal-dev team. The outage continued after the initial certificate renewal because the load balancer (LB-PROD-DC1) was still presenting an outdated certificate chain, blocking normal internal application access until the full chain was corrected and reloaded.

Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service outage

Users were trying to access the internal web service at www-internal.example.com (VIP 10.42.16.80 on LB-PROD-EAST-02), but browsers displayed certificate warnings and dependent API integrations failed TLS validation with "x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid." The outage was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office around 06:20 UTC on 2025-12-21 and quickly confirmed by multiple teams in us-east-1. Both interactive UI access and automated internal service calls (including the deployment pipeline used by the internal-devops group) were blocked until the expired leaf certificate and load balancer chain were corrected. Ticket opened by DevOps lead Rajesh Kapoor (EMP-40291).

Expired TLS certificate caused Internal Web Service TLS outage

Internal users and automated monitors at the Denver data center were trying to reach the Internal Web Service endpoint (internalweb.corplabs.internal) over TLS, but the endpoint began presenting certificate warnings and failing health checks overnight starting around 03:45 UTC on 2025-12-22. Clients reported ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID and TLS handshakes failed across multiple paths, which made the service unavailable to dependent internal applications including the payroll portal and inventory management system.
